security_audit.summary: Most static import, URL, and backtick findings are Markdown or Go example false positives. The main risk is semantic: the skill explicitly teaches anti-bot evasion and labels that behavior as safe.

remediation.suggestion: Remove instructions to bypass Cloudflare or Akamai, stealth scripts, user-agent rotation, behavioral noise, and human-like input evasion.
Reclassify the skill risk and document authorized testing boundaries, rate limits, consent requirements, and prohibited target evasion.
Pin the Playwright Go installer version and tell users to review dependency changes before running installation commands.

content.value_statement: Go teams need reliable browser automation for dynamic sites and test flows. This skill provides Playwright Go patterns for contexts, logging, timeouts, and sessions.
actual_capabilities: Explains Playwright Go setup with browser launch, context creation, and page creation.
Shows how to structure automation with one browser and separate browser contexts.
Recommends Zap logging for navigation, clicks, inputs, and error traces.
Provides timeout, cleanup, and panic recovery guidance for stable automation.
Includes session save and load concepts for cookie-based workflows.
Provides examples for mouse and typing interaction helpers.
limitations: Requires Playwright Go drivers and browser binaries to be installed before use.
Full browser automation can consume significant CPU and memory.
Does not solve CAPTCHA challenges or guarantee access to protected sites.
Anti-bot evasion guidance must be removed or limited to authorized testing.

use_cases.title: Automate Dynamic Web Tests
use_cases.description: Create Go test flows for sites that require a real browser and JavaScript execution.

use_cases.title: Prototype Browser Workflows
use_cases.description: Draft Playwright Go scripts that open pages, create contexts, and collect visible page data.

use_cases.title: Improve Automation Reliability
use_cases.description: Add logging, cleanup, explicit timeouts, and context isolation to existing scripts.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Script
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a simple browser task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a Go Playwright script that opens a page, waits for content, and closes resources cleanly.

prompt_templates.title: Add Logging and Timeouts
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Playwright Go workflow and recommend Zap logging, explicit timeouts, and defer cleanup points.

prompt_templates.title: Design Context Isolation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Playwright Go architecture that uses one browser instance and separate contexts for independent sessions.

prompt_templates.title: Harden an Existing Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my Playwright Go automation plan for resource leaks, weak error handling, unsafe target behavior, and missing authorization checks.

output_examples.input: Create a first Playwright Go automation plan.
output_examples.output: A concise setup plan with browser launch steps, context creation, page navigation, logging points, and cleanup reminders.

output_examples.input: Review an unreliable browser automation workflow.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review that calls out missing timeouts, missing defer cleanup, weak logging, and risky retry behavior.
An architecture summary that separates browser lifetime, context lifetime, session data, and worker responsibilities.

best_practices: Use one browser instance and separate contexts for isolated sessions.
Log every important navigation, click, input, error, and retry with structured fields.
Only automate sites where you have permission and follow target terms.
anti_patterns: Do not create a new browser process for every small task.
Do not rely on default timeouts for critical actions.
Do not use stealth or evasion patterns against protected third-party sites.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design Go browser automation using the Playwright Go library.

faq.question: Does it install Playwright automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents installation needs, but users must run and review installation commands themselves.

faq.question: Can it help with web testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It is useful for browser tests that need JavaScript rendering and real page interaction.

faq.question: Can it scrape websites?
faq.answer: It can guide approved data collection workflows, but users must respect authorization, robots policies, and site terms.

faq.question: Does it include CAPTCHA solving?
faq.answer: No. The source states that it does not include built-in CAPTCHA solving capabilities.

faq.question: What is the main security concern?
faq.answer: The source includes anti-bot evasion guidance that should be removed or limited to authorized testing.
